 Are schools open Election Day in Illinois? What's open and closed Tuesday 
 Election Day for the 2026 midterm election in Illinois takes place Tuesday, Nov. 3 
 By NBC Chicago Staff • 
 Published 1 hour ago • 
 Updated 1 hour ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 After votes are cast in an election, officials are responsible for carrying out a certification process in the following weeks to ensure true and accurate results.
 Election Day for the 2026 Illinois midterm election is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Is the day a federal holiday, and are any schools closed?
 Illinois law states that any school that doesn’t have instruction on Election Day can be used by local authorities as a polling place. And in many cases, schools across the states are closed in observance of the day. 
 Stream NBC 5 for free, 24/7, wherever you are.
   WATCH HERE 
 Illinois' largest school district, Chicago Public Schools, is closed to students on Election Day with no classes. Many suburban school districts are also closed Tuesday, including Wilmette District 39, Indian Prairie School District 204 in the western suburbs and Oswego Community Unit School District 308. 
 Some districts, private schools and universities may have still hold classes Tuesday, or have an Institute Day scheduled for staff.
 Under Illinois law, workers are permitted two hours of paid time off  to cast ballots on Election Day. 
 What else is open and closed on Election Day in Illinois? 
 Banks

 While some have tried to make Election Day a federal holiday in the past, they have not been successful thus far. As a result, many banks, federal facilities including courthouses, and most businesses will be open on Tuesday, according to officials.
 Illinois DMVs 
 Illinois Secretary of State Driver Services locations are closed on Election Day. 
 Illinois libraries 
 Many Illinois libraries are open on Election Day, and some even serve as polling places. 
 Is mail delivered on Election Day? 
 Since Election Day is not a federal holiday, all post offices will be open and mail delivery will proceed as normal.
